subject: Acme readiness: pipeline coverage sweep & commit signal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme readiness: pipeline coverage sweep & commit signal

Team —

Quick check-in on Acme (DEAL-2027-ACME-57). Finance is asking for a firm readiness signal for next quarter and we still have a coverage gap if we lose any of the two mid-stage commitments. Need everyone to update stage/confidence in HubSpot and call out any gating blockers by EOD today.

Action items (please reply inline):
- Update HubSpot stage to the most accurate value and set probability
- Add a one-line reason if confidence < 60%
- Confirm next touch with Acme and whether finance is looped in
- Attach any latest collateral (MAP, pricing, SOW drafts)

I've attached the latest opportunity map for reference: acme_opportunity_map_v2.xlsx (attachment).

Why now: finance needs a conservative coverage calculation for our quarterly forecasting call. If we can't move one of the mid-stage opportunities forward, we should plan a lightweight coverage mitigation (redistribution or temporary credit).

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme readiness: pipeline coverage sweep & commit signal

On Wed, Jun 9, 2027 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick check-in on Acme (DEAL-2027-ACME-57).

Quick numbers from my side: the two opportunities we were worried about are 'Acme Platform' (SQL -> Negotiation) and 'Acme Expansion' (Demo -> Eval). Probabilities I just set in HubSpot: 55% and 40% respectively.

I attached a one-page commit summary (commit_summary.pdf) with expected close windows and the last customer signal (technical stakeholder notes). The primary blocker is a procurement timeline mismatch — they plan a finance review the week of 6/21.

If we assume both convert at current probabilities, we still fall ~18% short of the target for the quarter. I recommend we: 1) prioritize a finance-aligned meeting next week, 2) offer a short pricing runway (one-time credit) as a lever if they need tighter cost predictability.

—Ben

ben@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme readiness: pipeline coverage sweep & commit signal

Thanks Ben — saw your updates. My confidence call: Acme Platform is high intent but procurement is the gating factor. I spoke to the technical DM and they asked for a clear mutual action plan that maps milestones (security review, SOW review, procurement approval) with owners and target dates.

I'm drafting a two-week MAP and will attach a lightweight version to share with the customer. Plan:
- Draft MAP to customer by EOD (mutual_action_plan.md)
- Coordinate finance@acmecorp.com to lock purchase window (target week of 6/21)
- If finance needs pricing certainty, we can offer a 60-day invoicing option or a small implementation credit (decision point at exec approval)

I'll update the HubSpot close date to reflect procurement cadence and add a 1-line note with P50/P90 scenarios.

Karthik
Head of Mid-Market Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmecorp.com>
Cc: finance@acmecorp.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Pipeline readiness & mutual action plan

Hi Alice — following up from our internal readiness sweep. Thanks again for the productive demo last week. To make finance and procurement cycles smoother on your side, we've prepared a short mutual action plan that maps the remaining steps, owners, and target dates.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.md (lightweight). Also linking the shared MAP here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Acme-MAP-Shared

Suggested immediate next steps:
- Can finance@acmecorp.com confirm a preferred PO cadence (net-30, net-45 or invoicing option)?
- Targeting a procurement review week of 6/21 — can you confirm availability for a 30-minute sync with our finance lead?
- If helpful, we can provide a one-time pilot credit to compress approval timelines (we would need an exec approval).

If you prefer, I'll route a brief pricing one-pager to the finance mailbox (attached: pricing_onepager.pdf). Let me know the best time for the sync and who from your team should be present.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme - Pipeline readiness & mutual action plan

Marissa — thanks for the MAP and for pulling this together.

Finance confirms a preference for net-45 but open to a short invoicing trial for the pilot. We're available for a procurement sync on 6/22 at 10:00am PST — finance will be on the call. Please send the pricing one-pager ahead of the meeting so finance can review.

Quick ask: can you include a short section in the MAP that clarifies the support handoff and escalation SLA for the pilot period? That will help procurement sign off faster.

I'll wait for the pricing doc and the updated MAP.

Thanks —
